q-79426.worked_solution:
To graph the function $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and stretch it by factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $6.$

q-79429.name: Question 2
q-79429.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3,-12)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)?$
q-79429.worked_solution:
The function $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $6.$

Therefore, the point $(3,-12)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $(6\cdot 3,-12)=(18,-12),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(\frac{1}{6}x).$

Question 2
?

The point P with coordinates (3,−12) lies on the curve y=f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(16x)?

a
(3,−72)
b
(18,−12)
c
(3,−2)
d
(12,−2)
e
(12,−12)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function y=f(16x) represents a stretch of the function y=f(x) by a factor of 6 parallel to the x-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the x-coordinates of all points on y=f(x) by 6.

Therefore, the point (3,−12) on f(x) is mapped to the point (6⋅3,−12)=(18,−12), and this point must lie on the graph of y=f(16x).
